title: Audible
html_source:
Stephen associates the audible with nacheinander (things happening in order, one after the other in time). Traditionally, what applies to the audible would apply to written works also. So, we understand a novel by what happens in time (nacheinander). But is that the only way to understand audible works?

Stephen immediately thinks of nebeneinader (things next to each other in space). This is how we understand pictures (paintings, drawings, maps). Can this be presented in a novel also?
